concepts.name: Nucleolus
forms: A nucleolar granular component containing multiple dense fibrillar components and fibrillar centers.
A nucleolus inside a nuclear envelope, with its smaller internal components shown schematically.
concepts.limits: Membraneless nucleolar organization is schematic and not to scale. Subcompartment number, shape and composition vary with species and state; no ribosome-production rate or molecular stoichiometry is encoded.

concepts.name: Nuclear Speckle
forms: Several irregular nuclear speckles positioned separately from a nucleolar context cue.
A single irregular membraneless speckle with illustrative RNA–protein material.
concepts.limits: Speckle contours and internal marks are illustrative. They do not specify SON or SRRM2 localization, RNA sequence, active splicing events, or a measured number of bodies. The outline delimits a condensate, not a lipid membrane.

concepts.name: Condensed Chromosome
forms: A replicated condensed chromosome with similar-length arms and a central centromere cue.
A replicated condensed chromosome with unequal arm lengths and an offset centromere cue.
concepts.limits: An isolated replicated chromosome schematic, not a karyotype or chromosome-specific anatomy. The X-like silhouette is not a universal chromosome shape or a depiction of DNA helix scale.

concepts.name: Primary Cilium
forms: A single membrane-covered ciliary projection above an apical surface, with an axonemal cue and basal body.
A curved primary cilium with continuous surface membrane, an axonemal cue and a basal body.
concepts.limits: A longitudinal primary-cilium schematic, not a motile cilia brush border. Microtubule number, ciliary pocket geometry, length, bending mechanics, transition zone and species are not specified.

concepts.name: Caveola
forms: A flask-shaped plasma-membrane invagination with a narrow surface connection and caveolar coat cues.
One surface-connected caveolar invagination beside neighboring caveolar profiles.
concepts.limits: A generic caveolar morphology. Coat marks do not imply clathrin, caveolin stoichiometry or a fully detached vesicle; neighboring profiles do not establish their three-dimensional connectivity.

concepts.name: Clathrin-coated Vesicle
forms: A detached closed vesicle membrane, internal cargo cues and a surrounding polygonal coat.
A polygonal clathrin-cage cue surrounding a closed membrane profile.
concepts.limits: A detached coated-vesicle schematic, distinct from the existing surface-connected endocytic pit. Cage polygon count, adaptor identity, cage topology, cargo and diameter are not molecularly resolved or measured.

concepts.name: Extracellular Vesicle
forms: A closed extracellular lipid vesicle with illustrative internal cargo and surface components.
A multivesicular-endosome profile continuous with the plasma membrane, with internal and released vesicle cues.
concepts.limits: An isolated EV silhouette cannot establish endosomal biogenesis or justify calling an observed vesicle an exosome. Only the release form illustrates an endosomal-origin model. No size, marker specificity, cargo sequence, purity, subtype or uptake mechanism is asserted.

concepts.name: Phagolysosome
forms: A membrane-bounded phagolysosome containing a rod-shaped cargo cue and lysosomal enzyme cues.
A membrane-bounded phagolysosome containing several cargo fragments and lysosomal enzyme cues.
concepts.limits: A mature degradative compartment schematic, not a demonstration of acidification, successful killing, a bacterial species or a measured digestion stage. Enzyme dots are illustrative and have no molecular count.

concepts.name: Lamellipodium
forms: A migrating cell with a broad leading-edge sheet and branched actin cues.
An enlarged broad membrane sheet supported by several branched actin cues.
concepts.limits: A thin sheet-like protrusion schematic. Branch geometry, filament number, force, motility direction and Arp2/3 position are not measured. This form contrasts with a filopodium but does not assert mutually exclusive protrusion types.

concepts.name: Filopodium
forms: A cell with a slender membrane protrusion supported by parallel actin-bundle cues.
An enlarged finger-like membrane protrusion containing parallel actin filaments and crosslink cues.
concepts.limits: A generic filopodial morphology; filament number, crosslinker identity and orientation, force, receptor localization and motility are not specified. The slender protrusion is not a microtubule-based cilium.

concepts.name: Necrotic Cell
forms: A swollen cell with a breached plasma membrane, vacuolization cues and released material.
An irregular cell remnant with discontinuous borders and separated cellular debris.
concepts.limits: A generic lytic morphology, not a diagnosis or a distinct upstream death pathway. Necrosis-like appearance alone cannot distinguish accidental injury, necroptosis, pyroptosis, ferroptosis or late apoptotic secondary necrosis.

concepts.name: Ferroptotic Cell — Schematic
forms: A cell with symbolic membrane lipid-damage marks and small compact mitochondrial cues.
A cell with symbolic lipid-damage marks and emphasized compact mitochondria with sparse cristae cues.
concepts.limits: A mechanism-oriented schematic, not a diagnostic appearance. Colored marks mean illustrative lipid peroxidation, not a particular stain or iron count; ferroptosis requires appropriate biochemical, genetic or pharmacological evidence. Mitochondrial changes vary by model.

concepts.name: Pyroptotic Cell — Schematic
forms: A swollen cell bearing several symbolic gasdermin pore rings.
A pore-bearing cell with a disrupted membrane and released contents.
concepts.limits: Gasdermin ring symbols communicate a mechanism, not microscopy-resolved pore number, scale, subunit count or a diagnostic morphology. The drawing does not specify inflammatory caspase, gasdermin family member, cytokine identity or experimental evidence.

concepts.name: Necroptotic Cell — Schematic
forms: A swelling cell with abstract membrane-associated MLKL cues and an intracellular vacuole cue.
An irregular swelling cell with membrane-associated MLKL cues, a breached border and released material.
concepts.limits: An MLKL-associated mechanism schematic. The clustered marks do not specify MLKL oligomer stoichiometry, a resolved pore structure, RIPK1 dependence or a diagnostic morphology; pathway identity requires independent evidence.

concepts.name: Anoikis — Schematic
forms: A detached cell above extracellular matrix with condensing chromatin and disengaged attachment cues.
A detached blebbing cell above extracellular matrix with chromatin fragmentation and an apoptotic-body cue.
concepts.limits: Anoikis means apoptosis associated with loss of appropriate matrix attachment. Detachment alone does not imply death; anchorage dependence and susceptibility vary by cell type, transformation state and culture conditions. Fragment number and timing are illustrative.

concepts.name: DNA Damage Foci
forms: A nuclear context containing dispersed illustrative DNA damage-response foci.
A nuclear context containing two local clusters of illustrative DNA damage-response foci.
concepts.limits: Puncta are illustrative response-factor domains, not direct counts of DNA breaks, mutations or repair events. Gamma-H2AX, 53BP1 and yeast repair-factor patterns are not interchangeable measurements; the generic drawing assigns no marker identity or measured coordinates.

concepts.name: Replication Stress
forms: A parental DNA fork and two nascent DNA strands with an illustrative impediment cue.
A replication-fork schematic with an additional paired nascent-strand arm at the junction.
concepts.limits: A DNA topology schematic, not sequence, replication speed, specific replisome proteins or a demonstrated cellular state. Fork reversal is one response to stress and is not inevitable; a stalled Y fork does not itself prove reversal or DNA breakage.

concepts.name: ER Stress / Unfolded Protein Response
forms: An ER lumen containing unfolded protein cues and a paired membrane-associated stress-sensor cue.
An ER lumen containing unfolded protein cues with a clustered stress-sensor and illustrative outward signal cue.
concepts.limits: An IRE1-informed generic ER stress schematic, not the complete PERK, IRE1 and ATF6 branches. Sensor count, activation, XBP1 splicing, apoptosis and adaptive outcome are not measured or implied by shape alone. The arrow indicates a generic downstream signal.

concepts.name: Mitochondrial Fission
forms: An elongated mitochondrion narrowed at a central division-machinery cue.
Two separated daughter mitochondrial profiles with division-machinery disassembly cues.
concepts.limits: A generic division event, not complete DRP1, actin or ER-contact anatomy. Ring geometry, cristae number, mtDNA partitioning, fragment size, rates and stress or death outcomes are not specified. Separation is shown as a state rather than a measured motion.

concepts.name: Mitochondrial Fusion
forms: Two mitochondrial profiles approaching a symbolic tethered membrane contact.
A continuous elongated mitochondrial profile with a localized joining-site cue.
concepts.limits: A membrane-joining schematic, not resolved outer- versus inner-membrane fusion or evidence of content mixing. Tether identity, mitofusin or OPA1 stoichiometry, membrane potential, rate and biological outcome are not specified. Arrows indicate approach.
